successors.name: Almohad Caliphate
successors.text: Marrakesh, Fez and the Moroccan core fell to the Almohads in 1146-1147 and the Balearic Islands of the Banu Ghaniya in 1203

ledger.x: 1054: the Almoravids take Sijilmasa and Awdaghust.

ledger.cp: Aghmat (rulers not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1060: the Almoravids hold the Barghawata country.
1070: Marrakesh founded as the new capital.

ledger.cp: Fez (rulers not named on the page)
Tangier and Oujda (rulers not named on the page)
Tlemcen (holder not named; the Tlemcen timeline lists the Hammadids)

ledger.x: 1082: Oran and Tenes taken, with the Hammadid country round them.
1087: Abu Bakr ibn Umar dies and the Saharan wing parts from the Moroccan empire.
ledger.cp: Southern Almoravids of the Adrar (Azuggi): the descendants of Abu Bakr ibn Umar and of his brother Yahya

ledger.x: November 1094: Lisbon, Sintra and Santarem pass from Alfonso VI to the Almoravids.
1104: the occupation of Algiers is taken to end with the peace treaty with the Hammadids; the Almoravid page is silent on Algiers after 1082 (bridging judgement).
1110: Zaragoza taken, the last independent taifa.

ledger.cp: Balearic Islands (last local ruler Mubashir al-Dawla)

ledger.x: 1144: southwestern Iberia lost to the Muridun.
ledger.cp: Muridun of Ibn Qasi (Silves, Mertola, Beja, Evora)

ledger.x: 1145: Malaga and Jaen become second taifas.
ledger.cp: second taifas of Malaga and Jaen (no Cliopatria row)

ledger.x: 1147: Marrakesh falls and the dynasty with it.
1147: the dynasty of Yusuf ibn Tashfin ends at Marrakesh; its Balearic branch, the Banu Ghaniya, 'a branch of the Almoravids', continues.
1147: southern Morocco goes with the dynasty.
1147: Algeciras and Tarifa fall to the Almohads.
15 March 1147: Santarem falls to Afonso I of Portugal.
25 October 1147: Lisbon falls to Afonso I and the crusaders.
1149: the last Almoravid land outside Granada is bridged out.
ledger.cp: Castile, Aragon, Portugal and the Almohads (not apportioned on the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1184: the Banu Ghaniya, claiming to be 'heir of the Almoravids' under the Abbasid caliph, invade the Almohad east.
1185: the Almohads retake the Balearic Islands.

By 1187: Abdallah ibn Ishaq recaptures the Balearic Islands from the Almohads ('Recaptured the islands from the Almohads by 1187'); the page gives no date or method, so the year is the page's latest and the keyframe starts there.
1203: the Almohads take the Balearic Islands.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the Barghawata
wars.outcome: Almoravid victory: 'By 1060, however, they were conquered by Abu Bakr ibn Umar and were forced to convert to orthodox Islam'; Abdullah ibn Yasin was killed in the fighting in 1058 or 1059.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the northern Maghreb
wars.outcome: Yusuf ibn Tashfin's conquests: Fez 1070 (or 1069/1074/75), Tangier and Oujda 1079, Tlemcen 1080/81, Nekor 1080-81, Algiers, Tenes and Oran 1082-83, Ceuta 1083.

wars.name: Battle of Sagrajas (az-Zallaqah)
wars.outcome: Almoravid victory on 23 October 1086: 'Alfonso was soundly defeated'.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the taifas
wars.outcome: Granada Sept 1090, Cordoba and Seville 1091, Almeria late 1091, Murcia 1092, Badajoz 1094, Valencia 1102, Zaragoza 30 May 1110 ('ending the last independent Taifa kingdom').

wars.name: Hammadid-Almoravid war over Tlemcen
wars.outcome: The Hammadid page: 'In 1103-1104 the Hammadids defeated the Almoravids and took control of Tlemcen'; the Almoravid page: 'in 1104, they signed a peace treaty with the Hammadids'.

wars.name: Siege of Zaragoza (1118)
wars.outcome: Alfonso I of Aragon took Zaragoza: the siege 'began on 22 May and, after no significant reinforcements arrived, it surrendered on 18 December'.

wars.name: Battle of Cutanda
wars.outcome: 'A serious defeat at the Battle of Cutanda in 1120' for the Almoravids; no zone named on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Fraga
wars.outcome: 'The most significant was the Battle of Fraga in 1134': listed among the setbacks of the Almoravids' decline; no territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the Almoravids
wars.outcome: Ibn Tumart's base at Tinmel 'around 1124'; the Almoravids crush the Almohads at Marrakesh in April or May 1130; Tlemcen 1144, Oran 1145, Fez 1146, Marrakesh 1147 after an eleven-month siege.

wars.name: Banu Ghaniya campaigns in Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: The Banu Ghaniya took Bougie, Constantine and Algiers and much of Tunisia; 'Yaqub al-Mansur reconquered Ifriqiya in 1187-1188'; raids continue to 1237/38.

wars.name: Siege of Lisbon (1147)
wars.outcome: Portuguese-crusader victory: Santarem taken on 15 March 1147 and Lisbon on 25 October 1147 after a siege begun on 1 July; both cities leave the Almoravids.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Almoravid al-Andalus
wars.outcome: The Muridun revolt of 1144 and the second taifas of 1144-1147 end Almoravid rule in most of the peninsula; the Almohads take Algeciras and Tarifa (1147), Seville (1148), Cordoba (1149) and defeat the Almoravids in Granada in 1155, after which the remnant…

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines exist for the whole life: the Saharan homeland is nomad country with no boundary, the Andalusian frontier with the Christian kingdoms moves with campaigns (Zaragoza lost 1118), and the sources name cities, not…
